context.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor and provides case management for suspicious payments. It ensures high-performance fraud prevention while meeting strict regulatory, security, and auditability constraints.

## Key Elements
*   **Payment Gateway / Core Processing Platform:** Upstream external system.
*   **Identity Provider (IdP):** External authentication provider.
*   **SIEM / Compliance Archive:** External storage sink.
*   **Fraud Analyst & Risk Officer:** Internal actors.
*   **Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System:** Core AWS-hosted system containing API Gateway, ECS Fargate scoring services, Redis cache, and S3 Object Lock storage.

## Relationships
*   **Payment Gateway to Core System:** Submits authorization requests via gRPC over mTLS.
*   **Fraud Analyst to Core System:** Manages cases and reviews transactions via HTTPS over TLS 1.3 protected by AWS WAF.
*   **IdP to Core System:** Authenticates users via OIDC / OAuth2.
*   **Core System to SIEM:** Exports compliance and audit logs asynchronously via AWS EventBridge / Kinesis.

## Technology Stack
*   **AWS ECS Fargate:** Selected for compute orchestration to minimize operational overhead for a 3-engineer team while supporting 3,000 TPS.
*   **AWS S3 with Object Lock:** Chosen for tamper-evident storage to satisfy the 7-year audit retention constraint (R-06).
*   **Redis Cache:** Deployed locally for high-performance fail-open heuristics, supporting the 1-minute availability requirement (R-07).
*   **AWS Secrets Manager:** Used for secure secret management with automatic rotation.

## Rationale
This architecture uses fully managed AWS services to stay within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and operational capacity of a three-engineer team. It enforces strict separation of concerns, tokenization, and multi-layered resilience to satisfy PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and sub-50ms P99 latency requirements.

containers.analysis:
## Overview
[Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud and manages analyst reviews. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance, explainable auditability, and <50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS within a €25,000 monthly AWS budget.]

## Key Elements
[Fraud Analyst, Risk Officer, Fraud Operations Manager, Payment Gateway, Identity Provider (IdP), SIEM / Compliance Archive, API Gateway (Envoy), Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go + ONNX on ECS Fargate), Case Management Backend, Web Application (React SPA), Audit Log Worker, Redis (ElastiCache), AWS Aurora PostgreSQL (Immutable Ledgers), Amazon SQS, AWS S3 / CloudFront]

## Relationships
[Payment Gateway to API Gateway via mTLS/HTTPS, API Gateway to Real-Time Scoring Engine via gRPC/HTTP2, Real-Time Scoring Engine to Redis via TCP/RESP, Real-Time Scoring Engine to Audit Log Worker via Amazon SQS, Audit Log Worker to AWS Aurora PostgreSQL via IAM-authenticated TLS, Web Application to Case Management Backend via REST/GraphQL over HTTPS, Case Management Backend to Identity Provider via OAuth 2.0 / OIDC]

## Technology Stack
[AWS ECS on Fargate for container orchestration with low operational overhead, Go and ONNX Runtime for high-performance stateless scoring, Node.js/Spring Boot for case management workflows, Redis (ElastiCache) for low-latency feature caching, AWS Aurora PostgreSQL with immutable tables for 7-year tamper-evident audit storage, React SPA on S3 and CloudFront for analyst UI, Terraform and GitHub Actions for zero-downtime GitOps deployments]

## Rationale
[This architecture separates high-throughput real-time scoring from human review workflows to meet strict P99 latency SLAs. Using managed AWS services and stateless containers optimizes operational simplicity for a three-engineer team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS data boundaries.]

API Gateway (Envoy).analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations to detect and prevent fraud. It processes transactions under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 constraints while providing case management for fraud analysts.

## Key Elements
- API Gateway (Envoy)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, ONNX Runtime, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js / Spring Boot)
- Web Application (React SPA, AWS S3, CloudFront)
- Audit Log Worker (Go)
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL (PostgreSQL, AWS Aurora)
- Amazon SQS

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> API Gateway (Envoy): Submits payment authorization requests via mTLS/HTTPS
- API Gateway (Envoy) -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Forwards scoring requests via gRPC/HTTP2
- API Gateway (Envoy) -> Case Management Backend: Routes administrative and analyst traffic via HTTPS
- Case Management Backend -> AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Persists case data and decisions via TLS/PostgreSQL Protocol

## Technology Stack
- Envoy: High-performance C++ API Gateway for mTLS termination, local rate limiting, and circuit breaking
- AWS ECS Fargate: Serverless container execution for cost efficiency and minimal operational overhead
- Go & ONNX Runtime: High-performance scoring execution meeting sub-50ms latency requirements
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Secure, managed relational database supporting 7-year audit retention

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless containers and managed AWS services to fit a 25,000 EUR monthly budget and a 3-person engineering team. Envoy and Go components ensure sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 requests per second while maintaining strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening screens card-not-present payment authorizations for a mid-size payment processor and enables fraud analysts to review suspicious transactions. It ensures sub-50ms P99 latency and full PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance under a fixed budget of 25,000 EUR per month.

## Key Elements
- API Gateway (Envoy)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, ONNX Runtime, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Scoring Orchestrator
- Feature Assembler
- Inference Executor
- Model Hot-Loader
- Rule Evaluator
- Audit Telemetry Emitter
- Redis (AWS ElastiCache)
- Amazon SQS
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL

## Relationships
- API Gateway -> Scoring Orchestrator: Forwards scoring requests [gRPC over HTTP/2 with mTLS]
- Scoring Orchestrator -> Feature Assembler: Coordinates feature fetch [In-memory Go function call]
- Feature Assembler -> Redis (AWS ElastiCache): Retrieves features [TCP/RESP]
- Scoring Orchestrator -> Inference Executor: Executes model [In-memory CGO/ONNX]
- Scoring Orchestrator -> Rule Evaluator: Evaluates overrides [In-memory]
- Scoring Orchestrator -> Audit Telemetry Emitter: Enqueues audit log [Local channel / ring buffer]
- Audit Telemetry Emitter -> Amazon SQS: Publishes audit events [AWS SDK / SQS API]

## Technology Stack
- Go: Chosen for high concurrency and performance to achieve sub-50ms P99 latency.
- ONNX Runtime: Enables fast, in-memory machine learning model evaluation.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Provides managed container orchestration within budget constraints.
- AWS ElastiCache Redis: Delivers low-latency feature storage.
- Amazon SQS: Asynchronously buffers audit and telemetry events.

## Rationale
This architecture balances strict sub-50ms P99 performance requirements with robust 7-year auditability and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. Using stateless Go containers on AWS ECS Fargate ensures high availability and cost control for a three-engineer team.

Case Management Backend.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management Backend is a core Spring Boot service that empowers fraud analysts to efficiently review suspicious transactions while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. It manages SLA-driven queues, case states, and tamper-evident audit logs to satisfy long-term regulatory audit requirements.

## Key Elements
* Case Management API Controller (Spring MVC)
* Workflow & Assignment Service
* Data Access Repository (Spring Data JPA)
* Audit Ledger Client
* Metrics & Telemetry Interceptor (Micrometer/Prometheus)
* AWS Aurora PostgreSQL (Database)
* Amazon SQS (Message Queue)

## Relationships
* Web Application -> Case Management API Controller: Sends REST/JSON requests over HTTPS
* Case Management API Controller -> Workflow & Assignment Service: Invokes business logic [In-process]
* Workflow & Assignment Service -> Data Access Repository: Executes queries [JPA/JDBC over TLS 1.3]
* Data Access Repository -> AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Persists case states [JDBC/TLS with AWS IAM Auth]
* Workflow & Assignment Service -> Audit Ledger Client: Dispatches audit records [In-process]
* Audit Ledger Client -> Amazon SQS: Publishes cryptographically chained audit events [AWS SDK over HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Spring Boot (Java): Chosen for robust enterprise security controls and team operational efficiency
* Spring Security: Enforces OAuth 2.0 JWT validation and method-level RBAC
* AWS ECS Fargate: Container orchestration ensuring zero-downtime deployments within budget
* AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Relational storage with KMS encryption for PCI-DSS data compliance

## Rationale
This architecture uses a unified Java stack to optimize delivery for a three-engineer team while meeting strict security and auditability mandates. It isolates sensitive workflows and enforces cryptographic audit logging without exceeding the monthly cloud budget.

Audit Log Worker.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud prior to approval and provides case management for suspicious payments. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability within a fixed monthly infrastructure budget.

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analyst & Risk Officer
- Payment Gateway / Core Processing Platform
- Identity Provider (IdP)
- SIEM / Compliance Archive
- API Gateway (Envoy) (Envoy, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, ONNX Runtime, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Backend (Node.js / Spring Boot, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Web Application (React SPA, AWS S3, CloudFront)
- Audit Log Worker (Go, AWS ECS Fargate)
- Redis (ElastiCache) (Redis, AWS ElastiCache)
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL (PostgreSQL, AWS Aurora)
- Amazon SQS (Amazon SQS)

## Relationships
- API Gateway (Envoy) -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Forwards authorization requests [gRPC / TLS 1.3]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Redis (ElastiCache): Fetches sliding-window velocity counters [Redis TCP Protocol / TLS]
- API Gateway (Envoy) -> Case Management Backend: Routes analyst review actions [HTTPS / REST]
- Case Management Backend -> AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Reads/writes review cases and decisions [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / IAM-authenticated TLS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS: Publishes asynchronous decision and audit events [AWS SDK / HTTPS]
- Amazon SQS -> Audit Log Worker: Delivers asynchronous audit logs [SQS Polling]
- Audit Log Worker -> AWS Aurora PostgreSQL: Persists canonicalized, hash-chained logs into append-only partitioned tables [PostgreSQL Wire Protocol / IAM-authenticated TLS]
- Audit Log Worker -> SIEM / Compliance Archive: Forwards batched audit logs with local disk spooling [HTTPS / TLS 1.3 with pinned certificates]
- Web Application -> API Gateway (Envoy): Accesses frontend assets and backend APIs [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]

## Technology Stack
- **AWS ECS Fargate**: Container orchestration chosen for zero-server management overhead, aligning with the 3-engineer team constraint.
- **Go**: Language selected for high-throughput, low-latency components (Scoring Engine, Audit Log Worker) and minimal memory footprint.
- **ONNX Runtime**: Embedded inference engine for running fraud scoring models with sub-50ms P99 latency.
- **AWS Aurora PostgreSQL**: Relational database utilizing table partitioning to manage 7-year audit data growth efficiently.
- **Amazon SQS with DLQ**: Messaging queue providing asynchronous decoupling and zero data loss guarantees for compliance workflows.
- **AWS KMS**: Hardware-backed Key Management Service providing cryptographic keys for SHA-256 tamper-evident hash chaining.
- **AWS S3 & Glacier Flexible Retrieval**: Object storage tiered via lifecycle policies to archive audit logs for 7 years within the €25,000 monthly budget.

## Rationale
This architecture meets sub-50ms P99 latency and strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance by decoupling real-time scoring from asynchronous compliance logging. Leveraging serverless and managed AWS services minimizes operational burden for a three-engineer team while guaranteeing 7-year tamper-evident auditability.

    description: "Persists canonicalized, hash-chained logs into append-only partitioned tables in AWS Aurora PostgreSQL."
  - type: "component"

AWS Aurora PostgreSQL.analysis:
## Overview
- PostgreSQL relational database architecture built on Amazon Aurora to support the real-time fraud screening system.
- Provides tamper-evident audit logging, high-performance case management, and strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- AWS Aurora PostgreSQL (Database Container)
- Transaction & Case Repository (PostgreSQL relational tables)
- Audit Ledger (Append-only WORM tables with `pg_audit`)
- Partition Manager (`pg_partman` extension)
- Connection Pooler (PgBouncer / Aurora Proxy)
- Aurora Read Replica (Dedicated for case management and analytical queries)
- Amazon S3 Glacier Vaults (Cold storage for audit archives via AWS DMS)

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Connection Pooler: Persists decision metrics and audit logs [IAM-authenticated TLS 1.3]
- Case Management Backend -> Aurora Read Replica: Queries active fraud cases and analyst workloads [SQL/JDBC over TLS 1.3]
- Partition Manager -> Amazon S3: Offloads historical audit partitions older than 90 days [AWS KMS encrypted S3 API]
- Database Audit Ledger -> Amazon CloudWatch / SIEM: Streams `pgaudit` activity logs [Encrypted CloudWatch Log Stream]

## Technology Stack
- Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL (`db.r6g.large`): Selected for predictable baseline performance and cost control within the €25,000/month budget.
- AWS KMS (AES-256): Ensures encryption-at-rest and strict cryptographic integrity for S3 Glacier archives.
- PgBouncer / Aurora Proxy: Manages connection spikes and prevents connection exhaustion from ECS Fargate tasks.
- `pg_partman` & AWS DMS: Automates time-based partitioning and cold storage offloading to meet 7-year audit retention.

## Rationale
- The architecture guarantees sub-second analyst workflows and protects P99 scoring latency by isolating read replicas and implementing connection pooling.
- It satisfies PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year tamper-evident auditability constraints through IAM database authentication, column-level security, and KMS-encrypted WORM storage.

Amazon SQS.analysis:
## Overview
[The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes card-not-present payment authorizations to approve, decline, or flag suspicious transactions while enabling case management for fraud analysts.]

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analyst & Risk Officer (Users)
* Payment Gateway / Core Processing Platform, Identity Provider (IdP), SIEM / Compliance Archive (External Systems)
* API Gateway (Envoy) (Envoy)
* Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, ONNX Runtime, AWS ECS Fargate)
* Case Management Backend (Node.js / Spring Boot)
* Web Application (React SPA, AWS S3, CloudFront)
* Audit Log Worker (Go)
* Redis (ElastiCache) (Redis, AWS ElastiCache)
* AWS Aurora PostgreSQL (PostgreSQL, AWS Aurora)
* Amazon SQS Standard Queue (`fraud-audit-events-queue`) with DLQ (`fraud-audit-events-dlq`)

## Relationships
* Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS: Publishes audit events [AWS SDK v2 / HTTPS / SigV4 / SQS API via VPC Endpoint]
* Amazon SQS -> Audit Log Worker: Delivers audit events [SQS Polling via AWS SDK v2 / PrivateLink]

## Technology Stack
* AWS SQS: Managed message queuing to decouple scoring from audit logging and protect P99 latency (<50ms).
* AWS KMS (Customer Managed Key): Server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) with `aws:SecureTransport` for PCI-DSS compliance.
* AWS VPC Interface Endpoints (PrivateLink): Secure network transit preventing public internet exposure.

## Rationale
[This architecture guarantees strict 50ms latency and 7-year auditability by asynchronously decoupling non-critical logging tasks via secure queues. It stays well within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget and operational capacity of three engineers using fully managed AWS services.]
